what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat serious bacterial infections in adults, including infections in the lungs (hospital-acquired pneumonia), urinary tract, abdomen, and bloodstream. It works by killing bacteria that cause these infections. Relebactam helps imipenem work better against certain bacteria that have become resistant to antibiotics.
how_to_take: This medicine is given to you through an IV (intravenous) line directly into your vein by a nurse or healthcare provider in a hospital or clinic setting. You will NOT take this medicine by mouth. Each dose is given slowly over 30 minutes. Do not try to give this medicine to yourself at home unless your healthcare provider has specifically trained you and set up home IV therapy.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 500 mg of imipenem, 500 mg of cilastatin, and 250 mg of relebactam, given every 6 hours (4 times a day) for up to 5 to 14 days, depending on the type of infection. Your doctor may adjust your dose if you have kidney problems. Always follow the exact dose and schedule your doctor prescribes — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: Since this medicine is given by a healthcare provider in a medical setting, a missed dose is unlikely. However, if you are receiving this medicine at home through home infusion therapy and you miss a dose, give it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double up doses to make up for a missed one. Call your home infusion nurse or doctor if you are unsure what to do.
storage: This medicine is prepared and stored by pharmacy or healthcare professionals. If you are doing home IV therapy, store the prepared (mixed) solution in the refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C) and use it within the time frame your pharmacist tells you. Do not freeze the mixed solution. Keep the medicine away from light and out of the reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine if it looks cloudy, has particles floating in it, or if the container is damaged.
what_to_avoid: Tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL medicines you take, including vitamins and herbal supplements, before starting this medicine. Avoid taking valproic acid (Depakote) or divalproex sodium (a seizure medicine) while on this antibiotic, as this combination can cause seizures and make your seizure medicine less effective. Do not skip doses or stop treatment early even if you feel better — finishing the full course helps prevent antibiotic resistance. Avoid alcohol if your doctor advises it during your treatment.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you experience: seizures or convulsions; severe allergic reactions such as rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, trouble breathing, or dizziness; severe skin blistering or peeling; severe or watery diarrhea (which may be bloody) during or after treatment, as this could be a serious gut infection called C. difficile; confusion, unusual behavior changes, or hallucinations; signs of kidney problems such as little or no urination or swelling in your legs; or yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice). Also contact your doctor if your infection does not seem to be getting better after a few days of treatment.
when_it_works: You may start to feel better within the first few days of treatment, but it is very important to complete the entire course of antibiotics your doctor prescribed, even if you feel well. Most people with serious infections treated in the hospital see improvement within 3 to 7 days. Your doctor will monitor your progress with blood tests and clinical exams to make sure the medicine is working for you.
special_populations: Kidney problems: Your doctor will check your kidney function and may lower your dose or give doses less frequently if your kidneys are not working well. This medicine is not recommended for patients on dialysis unless no other options are available. Older adults (age 65 and over): Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects, especially nervous system effects like confusion or seizures; your doctor will monitor you closely. Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Use this medicine during pregnancy only if clearly needed, as directed by your doctor. Breastfeeding: It is not known if this medicine passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while receiving this medicine. Children: The safety and effectiveness of this specific combination (with relebactam) have not been established in patients under 18 years of age.
